We at Yara are part of a global network, collaborating to profitably and responsibly solve some of the world's key challenges - resource scarcity, food insecurity and environmental change.

About the Unit

Within Yara, Crop Nutrition and Biologicals Products R&D leads the development and innovation of our crop nutrition solutions. We generate scientific and agronomic insights through laboratory, greenhouse, and field trials; translate these into product concepts and development projects, and support the wider organization with robust, evidence-based knowledge.

We are seeking a curious, proactive, and impact-driven scientist to advance our product development and innovation pipeline for new fertilizers and sustainable technologies that complement and strengthen Yara’s premium crop nutrition portfolio. This role is an integral member of the Crop Nutrition and Biologicals Products R&D team and reports to the R&D Lead - Premium Products and Organics.

Scientist - Crop Nutrition Products (f/m/d)

Location: Dülmen, NW, DE
Area of Expertise: Research and Technology Product Development
Job Type: Permanent
Work mode (place): On-site + Home office
Job Requisition ID: 24724

Design and coordinate R&D projects focused on developing high-efficiency phosphorous (P) and nitrogen (N) fertilizer product candidates.
Plan, coordinate and execute internal and external research on agronomic efficiency, nutrient release, soil quality and the environmental impact of fertilizer product candidates.
Develop and implement methods to evaluate the mode of action and performance of new crop nutrition products.
Perform screening and proof-of-concept testing for products and technologies originating from scouting activities and third-party collaborations.
Represent Yara at scientific and technical events, industry associations, and forums related to new fertilizer technologies.
Collaborate with the Premium Products and Organics R&D Team and the broader Crop Nutrition and Biologicals Products R&D organization by contributing to additional projects as needed.

Master’s degree plus relevant applied research or industry experience in crop nutrition, soil science, fertilizers, or related fields. A PhD in agronomy, soil science, crop science, plant nutrition, plant physiology or a related discipline is a plus.
Deep understanding of N and P chemistry in soils, nutrient dynamics, and mechanisms of nutrient uptake, transport and assimilation in plants.
Strong scientific grounding in crop nutrition, soil processes, and agronomy, gained through academic research or professional R&D experience.
Knowledge of soil and fertilizer chemistry and plant physiological processes, with the ability to apply these concepts to product development.
Fundamental knowledge of fertilizer products (e.g., soil- and foliar-applied fertilizers, liquids, water-soluble fertilizers, fertigation products, coatings, and seed treatments) and application techniques/equipment.
Hands-on experience conducting laboratory, greenhouse, and/or field experiments, and proficiency in experimental design, analysis and interpretation of complex datasets.
Ability to translate scientific insights into practical recommendations for Yara’s premium crop nutrition products.
Collaborative mindset and ability to work in multidisciplinary and international teams.
Fluency in English; German is a plus.
The position is full-time, permanent, and based in Duelmen, Germany.

As a global organization we actively strive to reflect diversity in society. We therefore encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply. We are committed to creating a work environment that fits gender equality.

Permanent employment contract with industry-standard remuneration
Flexible working options
30 days' vacation entitlement
37.5 hours of basic working time with time recording (flexitime)

Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences
PhD Position (f/m/x) in Statistical Physics/Quantitative Biology

Institute for Biological Physics | research group of Professor Berg

We are one of the largest and oldest universities in Europe and one of the most important employers in our region. Our broad range of subjects, the dynamic development of our main research areas and our central location in Cologne make us attractive for students and researchers from around the world. We offer a wide range of career opportunities in science, technology, and administration.

The research environment at the University of Cologne provides an excellent setting for interdisciplinary doctoral training. PhD students have access to a broad range of
graduate-level courses and training opportunities through the graduate school BCGS (see https://www.gradschool.physics.uni-koeln.de/). The group is also embedded in a vibrant research landscape, especially the Collaborative Research Centre CRC1310 Predicting Evolution, which brings together researchers from different fields to model and forecast evolutionary dynamics (see https://crc1310.uni-koeln.de/).
We are looking for highly motivated individuals who enjoy working in an international team at the interface between statistical physics and quantitative biology.

The University of Cologne promotes equal opportunities and diversity. Women will be considered preferentially in accordance with the Equal Opportunities Act of North Rhine-Westphalia (Landesgleichstellungsgesetz - LGG NRW). We also expressly welcome applications from all suitable candidates regardless of their gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, disability, age, personal orientation and identity.

The position is available form 1 October 2026 on a part-time basis (19,92 hours per week). The initial appointment will be for three years, funds for an extension are available.If the applicant meets the relevant wage requirements and personal qualifications, the salary is based on remuneration group 13 TV-L of the pay scale for the German public sector.
Please apply online with proof of the required qualifications (a CV, publication list if applicable, and research statement, one letter of recommendation should be sent directly by the recommender to bergj@uni-koeln.de) without a photo.
The reference number is Wiss2608-15. The application deadline is 15 September 2026.
For further inquiries, please contact Professor Dr Johannes Berg (bergj@uni-koeln.de) and take a look at our FAQs. YOUR TASKS

Depending on the interests and background of the successful applicants, projects will be available in cancer evolution, resistance dynamics, and statistical modelling of the immune system. Projects involve concepts and methods from equilibrium and non-equilibrium physics and are often based on experimental collaborations.

For more details see www.thp.uni-koeln.de/~berg.

The position includes a standard teaching load (in English or in German) of 2 SWS alongside research activities.
YOUR PROFILE

Applicants should have a Master‘s in physics with excellent grades, a strong background in statistical physics, and a genuine interest in biology.
WE OFFER

Broad research and training opportunities within the graduate school BCGS
Close research group integration/supervision
A diverse working environment with equal opportunities
Support in balancing work and family life
Extensive advanced training opportunities
Occupational health management offers
Flexible working time models
Opportunity to work remotely

Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region, the university can unfold to its full potential and showcase its innovative power and dynamism. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching and has great potential for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its institutes are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center - creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from every continent.
PhD student: Plant RNA Biology
The Wachter group at the Institute for Molecular Physiology (Faculty 10: Biology of Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz) investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants. Our recent work identified a structured mRNA element that regulates specific DEAD-box helicase genes and revealed their critical role in controlling alternative splicing. Intriguingly, these functions appear to be linked to unique C-terminal features of the respective helicases. As a member of an interdisciplinary and international research team, you will investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the splicing-regulatory activity of these DEAD-box helicases, with a particular focus on the functional relevance of RGG motifs, subcellular localisation, and their potential involvement in phase separation. In collaboration with the Weinberg group (University Halle-Wittenberg), you will also explore how helicase targeting of pre-mRNA structural elements may intersect with the binding of splicing regulators to determine splice site choice. Your research will employ a multidisciplinary approach that integrates molecular biology, RNA biochemistry, cell biology, and plant physiology, with Arabidopsis thaliana as the primary model system. You will benefit from extensive expertise, various core facilities, and a completely new research infrastructure. The PhD project is funded by the DFG and can be integrated in the international PhD programme (IPP) in Mainz.
Applying state-of-the-art techniques for gene-specific and genome-wide analyses of RNA biology, including transcriptome-wide profiling of alternative splicing and mapping of protein-RNA interactions
Employing in vitro and in vivo experimental systems to address different levels of complexity and advance our understanding of the biological functions
Contributing to teaching activities for Bachelor’s and Master’s students within our group
Assisting with organizational and administrative tasks
Presenting your research findings in oral and written form, including conference contributions, reports, and manuscripts

A successfully completed scientific university degree in Biology or in a related field
Practical experience with a spectrum of molecular methods
A background in plant molecular biology and/or RNA biology
Very good English language skills (at least level B2)
A fascination for science, very good communication, and teamwork skills

In addition to the general requirements according to public services law, applicants must meet the recruitment requirements stipulated in § 57 of the Hochschulgesetz of Rhineland-Palatinate.
Secure and transparent remuneration in accordance with the collective agreement of the federal states as well as additional benefits such as an annual special payment and company pension scheme
Discounted Deutschlandticket
Flexible working hours, 30 days' vacation and fair rules for balancing work and family life
Together, we are advancing science and society on this lively and dynamic campus
A wide range of offers for the development of your talents and perspectives
Opportunity to participate in general university sports programs

With nearly three decades of development experience and long-standing contributions to biologics supported by EMA and FDA approvals, Glycothera partners with biotech and pharmaceutical companies to advance development programs with scientific depth, precision, and consistency.

Scientist (m/f/d) Functional Assay
(full-time, permanent)

For our site in Jülich (Germany) we are looking for a highly motivated Bench Scientist to join our Functional Assay team. The main area of responsibility will be the development and execution of cell-based functional assays. In addition, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to work closely with the binding group to conduct Biacore/SPR assays.
Perform, evaluate and document experiments for method development of functional assays, including cell-based assays (e.g. potency, CDC, ADCC, ADCP, apoptosis assay, proliferation assay) and binding assays (e.g. Biacore/SPR) according to ICH guidelines.
Handle cell lines and primary cells (e.g. isolation, freezing, thawing, propagation, testing).
Analyze samples to support the development of therapeutic candidates across various departments/process steps.
Perform, evaluate and document functional assays for analytical similarity and comparability studies.
Draft regulatory documents, including SOPs, R&D-Procedures and development reports.
Support method validation and method transfer activities.
Take care of laboratory equipment (e.g., perform instrument maintenance and qualification) and support laboratory management tasks.
The role will be primarily lab-based.

B.Sc. in relevant scientific discipline (life sciences such as biology, biomedical sciences, biochemistry, biotechnology, etc.) with minimum 3-5 years of relevant work experience, or M.Sc. with 1-2 years of relevant work experience.
Experience working with mammalian cell lines under aseptic conditions, including culture initiation, propagation and cryopreservation is a must. Separation and purification of primary human cells is a plus.
Experience with potency and bioassay development (e.g., CDC, ADCC, proliferation, apoptosis) for monoclonal antibody analysis is required. Experience with other modalities is a plus.
Experience with relevant analytical methods (e.g., ELISA formats, Flow Cytometry) is required.
Experience with biochemical and biophysical methods for binding characterization (e.g., Biacore/SPR) is advantageous.
Attention to detail and precise work habits.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Proficient in using a PC and common Microsoft packages. Experience with specific laboratory instrumentation (e.g., Biacore T200 and 8K, MSD, Flow cytometer, microplate reader) and analysis software (e.g., SoftMax, Methodical Mind, MACSQuantify, Biacore Insight) is a plus.

You are a smart, proactive and solution-driven scientist with a hands-on attitude who is able to independently progress projects, prioritize tasks adequately and work against tight timelines. At the same time, you maintain a high-quality standard in your work, support the team and foster a sense of positivity. If this sounds like you, then join us in shaping what’s next!

jobs.description:
Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,500 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com
The Position
Join the dynamic Internal Consulting team at Boehringer Ingelheim! We're looking for innovative thinkers who are ready to shape our company's future.
As a Manager Consulting, you'll design, execute, and steer strategic initiatives within Boehringer Ingelheim. You'll independently coordinate project tasks, run data analyses, develop hypotheses and strategize solutions.
We value work-life balance, offering flexible work models and a location at the Headquarters in the Frankfurt Rhine-Main area.
This position is part time eligible with min. 80%.
Tasks & responsibilities

- As Manager Consulting, you will support in the design, execution and steering of strategic initiatives across businesses, functions, therapeutic areas, and regions within Boehringer Ingelheim.
- You will independently drive work packages within projects, generating strategic insights to enable informed decisions of top-level leaders.
- With your experience, you will run data analyses, develop hypotheses, find possible strategic paths and create actionable solutions to advance the organization.
- Having the successful outcome always in mind, you will track the progress and strategic alignment of projects and initiatives, in close collaboration with our business partners.

Requirements

- Excellent master's degree in sciences, economics or engineering (PhD or MBA a plus)
- Several years' experience with top-tier management consultancy, preferably with a focus on Pharma
- Track record of working on diverse national and international strategic projects
- Excellent critical thinking and analytical skills, with high attention to detail
- Great team player, with strong communication, presentation and stakeholder management skills
- C1 level English (written and verbal); additional languages are a plus

As part of our commitment to transparency and fairness, salary information will be shared during the recruitment process. We also offer a comprehensive benefits and wellbeing package.
Applications from persons with severe disabilities are warmly welcomed. In cases of equal qualifications, such applicants will be given preferential consideration in the selection process.
With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.

Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.

Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.

Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

Ready to contact us?

TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in Germany.

The new Center for Synergy of Systems (SynoSys) develops transdisciplinary approaches and methods in the fields of network science, data science and citizen science in order to conduct integrative research into complex phenomena at the interfaces between biomedicine, social sciences and life sciences. SynoSys will contribute to the emergence of a scientific vision for healthy human development in which physical and mental health are collectively considered in an increasingly digital and networked social and physical environment. As part of SynoSys the Research Group Computational Social Science is focused on the societal impact of digitalization. The group aims to better understand the dynamics of the complex dissemination of information online and its impact on culture, political behavior and democracy. We employ a broad set of methods, spanning agent-based modeling, time-series analysis, network science and natural language processing, to behavioral experiments in the lab and in the field. Data sources are diverse, either collected from online platforms, recruited participants or data donation approaches. To cover this spectrum, we aim for an inherent transdisciplinary approach and methodological innovation.
For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.

At the Center Synergy of Systems (SynoSys), the Research Group Computational Social Sciences offers, subject to the availability of resources, a position as

Research Associate / PhD Student (m/f/x)
(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E13 TV-L)

starting at the earliest possible date. The position is limited until September 30, 2029 and part of the project TRACE: Transparent Research on Algorithmic Content Exposure in Europe, which is funded by the Mercator Foundation. The period of employment is governed by the Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). The project will include scientific research and collaboration with the Institute of International Law, Intellectual Property and Technology Law at TUD to draft applications for accessing research data under the Digital Services Act Article 40. The core task will be to analyze the resulting data sets, focusing on the causal inference of algorithmic influence on content dynamics and offline outcomes. Other tasks include writing of scientific publications for relevant Journals, conducting detailed literature searches, participating in professional conferences, presenting the research and its projects.
university degree in an area of applied computational sciences
strong interest in working in a trans-disciplinary research environment at the interface of computer science, law and social sciences
methodological interest in platform data and causal inference
experience with the Digital Services Act and its data access rights
proficiency in data science applications in Python or R
ideally experience with NLP, large language models, longitudinal data and data privacy/anonymization
ability to work in a collaborative interdisciplinary environment
good command of spoken and written English
A unique opportunity to contribute to complex science research incl. topics like information propagation on social networks, the role of platform algorithms for societal risks.

30 days of paid annual leave and a year-end bonus payment; additional pension provision (VBL)

jobs.description:
A major focus of our research is the development of PROTACs as novel therapeutic approaches against cancer. Our research combines molecular genetics, biochemistry, cell biology, and cancer models. Recently published studies: Müller et al, EMBO Rep. 2026; Bhandare et al, Nucleic Acids Research, 2025; Vogt et al, Gut, 2024; Solvie et al, Nature 2022; Narain et al, Molecular Cell

Further information about our work can be found at:  www.biochemie-kiel.de/research-groups/wolf-group/  You will work on an ERC (European Research Council) or German Cancer Aid funded project. The research group is located at the Institute of Biochemistry, which is part of the Medical Faculty of the University of Kiel. The institute provides excellent facilities and state-of-the-art equipment, allowing you to perform cutting-edge experiments and acquire highly valuable skills for a future career in academia or industry. The department is located at the heart of the Kiel University campus, which provides a stimulating collaborative research environment with multiple research groups working on tumor biology and cellular proteolysis. We collaborate with numerous additional life science institutes in Kiel including the Kiel Oncology Network (KON), the Institute of Pharmacy and Kiel Life Science (KLS). - You are highly motivated and are eager to pursue a Ph.D. in the natural sciences with a medical focus.

- You have recently completed, or are about to complete, your Master's degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, cell biology, bioinformatics or a related field.
- You have excellent written and spoken English skills. Knowledge of German is desirable but not required.
- You enjoy working with young researchers in an international and collaborative team. The positions will start between December 2026 and March 2027 and the salary is based on TV-L E 13 (65%). In case of equivalent qualifications, disabled applicants will be preferentially considered.

jobs.description:
Introduction

The INM-Leibniz Institute for New Materials is an internationally leading center for interdisciplinary research on materials, and their exploitation in materials-based solutions for a sustainable world with increasing digitalization and medical needs. Our research integrates materials chemistry, biological engineering, physical analysis, process engineering and data science. We collaborate with academic and industrial partners all around the world.

A focus of our research are Engineered Living Materials (ELMs), an emergent class of materials at the interface between materials science and synthetic biology, with huge potential for sustainable innovation in different technological fields. The multidisciplinary component of our research requires intensive information and data exchange between multiple disciplines. We work on semantically structured data and interfaces, AI-driven workflows, and contribute to engaging the growing ELM community in digitalized research.

To support the digitalization of SynBio work within the context of ELM development, we are seeking a

Postdoctoral Researcher with expertise in Synthetic Biology (f/m/d)

and interest in data-driven research. The position is integrated in the collaborative network MaterialVital Hub , recently funded by the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) in collaboration with the Galaxy Community Hub . The candidate will be part of a team of experimental scientists and research data management experts at INM-Leibniz Institute for New Materials and Bioinformaticians at the University of Freiburg.

Contribute to the digitalization of synthetic biology workflows for ELM development in collaboration with SynBio researchers at INM.
Develop metadata schemas for typical synthetic biology steps and methodologies in ELM research which are transferable to electronic LabBooks and data platforms of relevance for other researchers within the MaterialVital Hub.
Contribute to the development of an ELM-dedicated ontology for interoperability within the MaterialVital Hub in cooperation with MaterialDigital Platform partners and the Galaxy Community Hub.
Support and promote digitalization of the ELM community within the MaterialVital Hub in close interaction with Galaxi Community Hub and MaterialDigital Platform and NFDI.
Attend workshops and disseminate your work within the ELM community by presenting at conferences and scientific events.
Document your work and report to project coordinators and stakeholders.

PhD degree in synthetic biology, biotechnology or related disciplines.
Experience as experimental researcher in combination with modelling or data-driven methods is ideal. Previous experience as data steward, or previous work within NFDI Consortia is of advantage. Knowledge in automated workflows for SynBio research is advantageous.
Interest in working with and for the digitalization of the ELM community.
Self-driven and hands-on personality. Organization and prioritization skills.
Very good communication skills in English.

An emergent research topic with multiple opportunities to contribute and interact with the growing community and contribute to its development at an early stage.
Direct access to and high visibility in the SynBio and ELM networks at national and international level.
An existing team with expertise and drive to move forward digitalization in ELM research. A well-structured on-boarding process and clear responsibilities.
A community-oriented, multifaceted work with great scope for creativity.
A highly professional and supportive working environment with an open and international culture.
Strong support of training and career development towards an outstanding profile as data scientist in synthetic biology research.
Flexible working hours and mobile working opportunity.
A family-friendly working place.
A EG 13 TV-L position (full time). A part time position is also possible.

jobs.employer_name: International Max Planck Research School for Living Matter
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about interdisciplinary research and eager to contribute to groundbreaking discoveries in the areas of biochemistry, structural biology, biophysics, cell biology, chemical biology and synthetic biology?

The International Max Planck Research School for Living Matter: from molecules to dynamics (IMPRS-LM) is a joint PhD program between the Max Planck Institute of Molecular Physiology, the TU Dortmund University, the Ruhr University of Bochum, and the University of Duisburg-Essen, located in the vibrant and multicultural Ruhr Metropolitan Area in Germany. The IMPRS-LM unites scientists from diverse disciplines to tackle a fundamental question in biology: How chemical components organize into the complex, dynamic systems we recognize as living cells? By combining experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches, our interdisciplinary team of molecular biologists, chemists and physicists explores the spatial and temporal dynamics of biochemical networks within the cellular environment. We welcome applicants with a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Biology, Biochemistry, Life Sciences, (Bio-)Physics, Chemistry, Computer Science, or related fields. The IMPRS-LM offers a unique, internationally recognized PhD training program designed to equip students with the interdisciplinary expertise needed to address complex challenges in cellular biology. Through a rigorous curriculum, hands-on research in world-class labs, and personalized mentorship, we empower students to become innovative, independent researchers ready to shape the future of science.

As a PhD student, you will benefit from:

Fully funded positions (via employment contracts with full social benefits)
Dedicated mentors who support your scientific and career development
An inclusive, international research community fostering collaboration and creativity
Access to state-of-the-art facilities and advanced technologies
A fully English-speaking program featuring lectures, advanced workshops, transferable skills training, and career development activities

Visit the IMPRS-LM website for more information about the program requirements, the application process, and the list of research group leaders currently offering positions.

The Max Planck Society is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace, providing equal opportunities to all employees, irrespective of gender, nationality, disabilities, religious or personal orientation. We strongly encourage applications from underrepresented groups.
